finding: Rob's direction: measure the build DAG once under DISABLED parallelism and derive per-command cost from the graph, instead of re-running every command. Serialised, aggregate step work and elapsed time coincide, so the sum of parts becomes sound; the stage graph with its joins and splits is already parsed by tools/build-observatory.py and already used for root-closure checking, and analysis.rocq-modules is the same idea one level down (per-module cost plus critical path). The caveat M2 records with it: a cost derived from serial stage costs plus the graph is a MODEL of wall time, not a measurement of it, so it belongs beside the measured per-command number rather than replacing it — which is the same aggregate-versus-elapsed line finding G drew. Its value is answering what a command SHOULD cost if the graph were exploited, which is the question R01 asks and cannot currently answer. ADOPTED INTO M2 by M2-SCOPE-AMENDMENT-TRACE-ACQUISITION: the canonical suite now acquires a minimal trace set and projects contained commands and stages from stable checkpoints and structured BuildKit events, instead of re-running a relation an exact containing trace already measures.

Rob's direction: the Docker stage graph should come from buildx, not from a hand-rolled parser. tools/build-observatory.py derives inter-stage edges by regex over FROM <stage> and COPY --from=<stage>; those are the only two ways an edge can exist and the derivation is mutation-covered, but it is still a second authority over a format the builder owns. The pinned runner carries buildx 0.20.1, which has --call (targets, outline); the host client is 0.13.1 and does not — which is irrelevant, since the query belongs in the pinned runner like every other tool, so the client version is pinned by digest rather than being whatever the developer happens to have. To verify before adopting: --call=targets certainly enumerates stages, but whether it exposes inter-stage EDGES in stable machine-readable form is unconfirmed — deliberately not tested during a measurement run, because evaluating the frontend touches a builder the suite is timing against. If edges are exposed, the parser goes; if only targets are, cross-check the derived stage SET against buildx's answer at minimum. VERIFIED 2026-07-31 during Repair 3: `docker buildx build --call=targets` run in the pinned runner (buildx 0.20.1; the host's 0.13.1 has no --call) enumerates all fifteen stages and agrees exactly with the coverage gate's count. So buildx can own the stage LIST. It does not emit the inter-stage EDGES, which is what the containment graph actually needs, so the regex derivation cannot simply be deleted — replacing it means taking edges from the LLB or a subrequest, and M3 should scope that rather than assume --call=targets is sufficient.
evidence_ids: no metric — a single-authority finding, not a timing one

finding: Sample multiplicity is fixed at three regardless of cost, and the observed variance shows that is backwards. In this run make.check under a .v edit measured 480/481/478s (0.6% spread) and warm no-op 347/344/342s (1.4%), while make.prove warm measured 1.6/1.8/1.6s (12%). So triplicate spends about sixteen extra minutes re-measuring a six-minute command that varies by three seconds, and takes the same three samples of a 1.6s command where variance actually matters. Rob's framing: an hour and a half of benchmarking to characterise a five-minute cold build is out of proportion. Candidate directions for M3, unranked: drive multiplicity from observed variance rather than a constant; or take one sample where a cheaper derived measurement already bounds the answer. Combined with R07 the disproportion is mostly self-inflicted rather than inherent. Why it went unnoticed is structural: make.observe is catalog-only because benchmarking the observatory through the observatory would recurse, so the one command whose cost nobody measures is the one that measures cost. Every other slow surface here has a number and a recommendation pointing at it; the measurer has neither, by construction. Any M3 remedy should say how the facility's own cost stays visible without measuring itself. ADOPTED INTO M2 by M2-SCOPE-AMENDMENT-TRACE-ACQUISITION, for canonical multiplicity and suite self-cost visibility only: canonical recording stores one sample per trace identity and repeats become ad hoc, and the observation retains the suite's own cost. Choosing a variance budget per metric remains M3.

finding: The observatory is part of the subject it observes, so any repair to tools/build-observatory.py changes the committed ref every sample's source digest was computed against, and recording rules R03/R04 then require the ENTIRE canonical suite be re-run from the new candidate. This is correct — an observation must describe exactly one committed state — but it makes the round trip for a one-line observer fix about two hours, which is what a value-dependent metric identity cost to close. M3 should decide whether the observer's own sources belong in the measured source view at all: the commands it measures do not read them, so a narrower per-command source view could keep the ref honest without forcing a full re-observation for an observer-only change. M2 records the tension; it does not decide it. M2 implements only the two parts this amendment requires — validating each trace fragment before the next begins, and exact same-subject resume. The reflexivity remedy itself, a narrower per-command source view, remains M3.
evidence_ids: no metric — an architectural finding about the observatory's own reflexivity

finding: The self-test constructs observations, headers and prior bundles BY HAND, so a fixture silently describes a shape the producer has left. Repair 3 hit this five times: a hand-supplied run_id that hid a producer defect for three canonical runs; controls pinned to a command whose classification changed, which made their perturbations inert; a checkpointer header without run_id; a prior-bundle fixture without run_id, which made a completeness control unable to fail; and a control coupled to a default fixture shape, which broke under an unrelated mutation and reported a sound rule as unprotected. The shape control added in Repair 2 catches a MEMBER that is missing or invented, and it has already earned its keep, but it cannot catch a field whose value is wrong or a fixture that selects the wrong sample. M3 should decide whether the synthetic observation, its headers and its bundles are built through the real producer functions end to end rather than assembled beside them.
evidence_ids: no metric — a test-architecture finding, not a timing one

finding: The observatory self-test prints a must-fail/must-accept partition it does not compute. `must_fail` counts only controls registered through `observed()` with a pinned reason, and must-accept is the remainder, so four controls that assert a REFUSAL are printed in the must-accept column: an unknown comparison selector, a cold sample with no observed stage state, a selected command with no sample and no reason, and concatenated builds with no invocation marker. Three of those four accept ANY ObservatoryError instead of pinning the reason they refuse for, which is the same masking shape that already cost this repair six R08 controls. What keeps this a mislabel rather than a hole is that the mutation harness names, per rule, which control must fail when that rule is deleted, so a control cannot silently pass on an unrelated error. Verified by inspection at 483791f, not estimated. Candidate direction for M3: register every control through one helper that records whether it must fail, and assert the two counts sum to the total, so a control that declares neither is a failure rather than a silent addition to the wrong column.
evidence_ids: no metric — a self-test reporting finding, not a timing one
